scene.note: The hut's money is kept exactly, rounded once to the penny, and printed the same on every computer.

steps.note: The morning's prices arrive as text, each exact as it is written.
Each price becomes an exact amount, and the amounts are added one by one into a total.
Two amounts written with a different number of decimal places are still the same money.
A group's fare starts from the adult fare and the number of people.
The whole amount is worked out first, the discount taken off, and only then rounded to the penny.
A bill shared between people is divided to the penny, rounding a half penny up.
An amount comes to the printer with however many decimal places it has.
The ticket shows a pound sign and two decimal places, the same on every computer.
An amount typed back in as text is read, and a text that is not an amount is refused by name.
